resources.string:
Do I need to open this app every day?
No. Once you've set your knobs and tapped Apply, they live permanently on the buds — they'll survive a case reset or reboot. Day to day, just wear both buds and quad-tap to turn BiCROS on or off. You only need this app when you want to change a setting or grab a log for troubleshooting.

How do I turn BiCROS on or off without my phone?
Quad-tap either earbud — they're linked, so either one works. Listen for the status tones below to know what's happening.

What do the status beeps mean?
• ENABLED — one short beep (~880 Hz) once BiCROS is actually up and running
• DISABLED — two short beeps when you turn it off (or a normal-sounding disconnect tone if the audio had already stopped on its own)
• NOT YET — a warning tone if you try to turn it back on while the last session is still finishing up shutting down. Just wait for the READY tone.
• READY — a normal-sounding "pairing success" tone. This means it's safe to turn BiCROS back on.
• OPEN FAIL — a "pairing failed" tone — the connection didn't come up. Try again once you hear READY, or reseat the buds in the case.

Where do my settings get saved?
Right on both earbuds themselves, the moment you tap Apply — no phone needed after that. Connect and hit Get anytime to pull your current settings back into the app.

Why can't I set the poor ear to Left?
The poor ear (the one doing the listening-for-you-on-the-bad-side job) can't currently be the earbud that's actively connected to your phone. By default, Right is the poor ear and Left is the one paired to your phone. If you set Left as the poor ear while it's also the one connected to your phone, BiCROS will refuse to turn on — this is a known limitation, not a bug you're triggering by accident.

What does my phone's volume rocker do while BiCROS is on?
It controls how loud the relayed sound from your poor side is — not your music, and not the natural sound in your good ear. Once you turn BiCROS off, the rocker goes back to controlling music like normal.

Why is the support log off by default?
Streaming a log over Bluetooth competes with BiCROS for the same connection, so it's best left off during normal use. Turn it on only when you're troubleshooting and need to send a log.

Why do my earbuds sometimes stop responding?
This BiCROS setup is a genuinely hacky workaround running on hardware that was never designed for it, so it crashes more often than not. If it happens: put both earbuds back in the case and wait until the LED turns solid red. Once it's red, take your good-side earbud out first and wait to hear the connected tone — only then take the poor-side earbud out too. The good-side earbud has to reconnect first, or BiCROS won't start up properly.

Why does turning BiCROS back on sometimes take a while?
This is expected, not a bug. The way this feature is built, it can take anywhere from about 20 seconds up to a minute to fully shut down before it's ready to turn back on — this is a real limitation of how it's implemented, and it was a deliberate tradeoff: making the shutdown wait longer instead of rushing it was the fix for making BiCROS reliable at all. If you hear the NOT YET tone, that just means it's still finishing up — wait for READY and it'll turn on normally.

Is it safe to turn the local ear mix all the way up?
There's a hard limit built in that the mix level can never exceed, specifically because an earlier version of this had a bug that caused real feedback (a loud howling sound) in someone's ear. That specific bug is fixed, and the ceiling stays in place as an extra layer of protection. Even so, it's a good habit to raise any volume-related setting gradually while you're wearing the buds, rather than jumping straight to the highest level.

Is this a hearing aid or medical device?
No. This is experimental, DIY firmware running on regular $70 consumer earbuds, and you're using it at your own risk. It hasn't been prescribed, fitted, or certified as hearing protection or a CROS/BiCROS medical device.
